Waterproofing: The UK Rider's Priority

In a country where it rains on average 156 days per year, waterproofing is not a luxury — it is essential survival gear. Getting soaked on a motorcycle at speed causes rapid heat loss that impairs concentration and reaction times. A properly waterproof jacket keeps you warm, dry, and safe throughout a long wet day in the saddle.

Understanding Waterproof Technologies

  • Laminated construction — Membrane bonded directly to outer shell. Water never penetrates past the first layer. Premium choice for touring.
  • Drop-liner construction — Membrane hangs inside as a separate layer. Outer fabric absorbs water, becoming heavy. Still waterproof but less comfortable in sustained rain.
  • Oversuit approach — Lightweight waterproof layer worn over regular jacket. Cheap and effective but flaps in wind and awkward to put on roadside.

Testing Waterproof Claims

Manufacturers rate waterproofing in millimetres of hydrostatic head. For motorcycle use in British conditions look for at least 10,000mm. Gore-Tex typically exceeds 28,000mm. Seam sealing is equally important — taped seams prevent water wicking through stitch holes that would otherwise defeat even the best membrane.

Top Waterproof Jackets for UK Touring

Rukka Navigatorr — Gore-Tex Pro Shell with fully taped seams. Tested in the worst Scottish weather, it keeps you bone-dry all day. The aqua seal on the main zip is outstanding against water ingress.

Klim Latitude — Gore-Tex laminate with proven pattern. Generous cut accommodates thermal layers. Storm collar and wrist closures are particularly effective against driving rain.

Rev It Defender 3 GTX — Excellent mid-price Gore-Tex option. The laminated construction punches well above its price point and the fit accommodates multiple body types.

Spada Metro — A budget laminated option that keeps water out surprisingly well. Not as durable as premium options but exceptional value for occasional wet-weather touring.

The best waterproof jacket is one you barely notice wearing. If you are constantly adjusting, fidgeting, or worrying about leaks, you will not enjoy the ride. Invest in genuine quality and forget about the weather.

Care and Maintenance

Reproof your jacket annually with Nikwax Tech Wash followed by TX.Direct to restore the DWR finish that causes rain to bead off. Never tumble dry Gore-Tex — heat damages the membrane. Hang dry away from direct heat and store unfolded to prevent crease damage to the waterproof membrane.

When to Replace Your Waterproof

Even the best waterproof jacket eventually loses its weather protection. If water soaks through despite reproofing, or if taped seams are peeling and delaminating, it is time for a replacement. Most quality waterproof jackets last five to eight years of regular touring use before the membrane degrades beyond effective reproofing. faq.q: What hydrostatic head rating do I need?
faq.a: For UK motorcycle use, look for a membrane rated at least 10,000mm of hydrostatic head, which resists the pressure of driving rain at speed. Premium membranes like Gore-Tex typically exceed 28,000mm. Equally important is seam sealing: taped or welded seams stop water wicking through the stitch holes that would otherwise defeat even a high-rated membrane.

faq.q: How do I reproof a waterproof jacket?
faq.a: Wash the jacket with a technical cleaner such as Nikwax Tech Wash to remove grime that blocks breathability, then apply a DWR treatment like TX.Direct to restore the water-beading finish. Never use ordinary detergent, which leaves residues that attract water. Never tumble dry Gore-Tex, as heat damages the membrane; hang it to dry away from direct heat instead.

faq.q: When should I replace a waterproof jacket?
faq.a: Replace it when water soaks through despite reproofing, or when the taped seams start peeling and delaminating. Most quality waterproof jackets last five to eight years of regular touring before the membrane degrades beyond effective reproofing. Budget for replacement as part of your long-term gear plan, as a failing waterproof leaves you cold and unsafe in British weather.

faq.q: Is a laminated jacket really better than a drop-liner?
faq.a: In sustained rain, yes. A laminated jacket bonds the membrane to the outer shell so water never gets past the first layer and the jacket stays light. A drop-liner hangs the membrane inside, so the outer fabric soaks up water and becomes heavy and cold even though you technically stay dry. For all-day UK touring the laminated approach is far more comfortable.
